5-Stage Pipelined RISC-V CPU
KAIST · SystemVerilog, ModelSim, EDA Playground
FPGA/ASIC-synthesizable 5-stage processor with full testbench verification. Directly relevant to FPGA-based high-speed data acquisition pipelines (OCT systems, digital back-ends).
  • Designed hazard detection and data-forwarding logic — eliminates pipeline stalls for all RAW dependencies across IF/ID/EX/MEM/WB stages
  • Verified with two full testbench programs (sort + forloop): 40 test cases all passing, 14,722 cycles, 147 µs simulation time
  • Real debugging evidence: caught forwarding bug mid-development — test #6 failed (0xfe8 vs 0xed8), traced via waveform, corrected and re-verified to 40/40
  • Architecture verified for both FPGA and ASIC synthesis targets via EDA Playground constraint checks
SystemVerilog ModelSim FPGA / ASIC hazard detection testbench suite timing verification
Sort testbench — 40/40 passed. All test cases #1–40 verified at 147,335 ns.
ModelSim waveform — sort program. CLK, RST, pipeline stage registers, forwarding signals.
Waveform — forloop program. IF/ID, ID/EX, EX/MEM, MEM/WB instruction words, PC write, flush signals across 450 ns.
Debugging evidence. Test #6 failed: 0xfe8 vs expected 0xed8. Mis-forwarded operand traced via waveform, corrected, all 40 tests subsequently pass.

Multi-Sensor Agricultural IoT Network
AXInvent · IoT Device Engineer Intern · Daejeon, South Korea
Full hardware lifecycle from part selection to field deployment. Master/slave LoRa mesh network for real-time environmental monitoring — built, debugged, and validated outdoors.
  • Part selection: CO2 sensor, soil moisture, wind anemometer, rainfall, soil temp — evaluated for outdoor endurance, power budget, and I2C/UART compatibility
  • System-level schematic design: pin mapping for all sensor interfaces, power distribution rails (5V, DC battery), LoRa module wiring across Arduino Uno slave nodes
  • Hardware bring-up and debugging: verified I2C bus timing with oscilloscope, traced and resolved NULL sensor readings by re-seating connectors and correcting pull-up resistor values
  • 3D enclosure design in Fusion 360 — weatherproof housing for master and slave nodes, optimized for cable routing and field serviceability
  • Full pipeline: slave Arduinos → LoRa → master → Raspberry Pi 4 → gRPC/HTTP/2 → server; validated with live acquisition logs
part selection schematic design hardware bring-up oscilloscope / DMM I2C / SPI / UART LoRa mesh Fusion 360 field-deployed
Device internals. Master node (Arduino + RPi4 + sensors) and slave node (Arduino + DC battery + LoRa antenna) in weatherproof enclosures.
Field deployment. Master + slave nodes deployed across open field — validating LoRa range, sensor readings, and battery endurance.
Communication pipeline. Slave Arduinos → LoRa → Master → USB → Raspberry Pi 4 → gRPC/HTTP/2 → AXInvent server.
Field test data. Air temp 27.6°C, wind 3.2 m/s, CO2 633–639 ppm, soil readings. NULL rows = sensor fault isolation targets during bring-up.

Ultra-Low-Power Smartwatch Firmware
KAIST · C, nRF5 SDK, Arduino Nano 33 BLE
End-to-end embedded firmware from power budget design to measured current draw. Demonstrates sensor integration, I2C protocol handling, and power state machines — core skills for implantable and surgical device electronics.

  • Implemented C firmware on nRF5 SDK managing gesture-driven UI, BLE sync, and multi-sensor polling windows with independent sleep cycles
  • Full bring-up loop: breadboard prototype → soldered assembly → current measurement → firmware power optimization

Digital Clock FSM in SystemVerilog
KAIST · SystemVerilog, EDA Playground
RTL implementation with three verified operating modes: normal time advance, time adjustment, and alarm set/clear. FSMs, flip-flops, counters, and MUX trees verified through full waveform analysis.
  • Designed alarm control FSM with set/clear inputs and output — edge transitions verified with testbenches
  • Verified hours, minutes, seconds tracking across all three modes via dedicated waveform analysis
